'''Sebastian Hiller''' is a German and [[Switzerland|Swiss]] [[Structural biology|structural biologist]] and [[Biophysics|biophysicist]]. He has been teaching and researching at the [[Biozentrum University of Basel|Biozentrum]] of the [[University of Basel]] since 2010.<ref name=cv>{{cite web |url=https://www.biozentrum.unibas.ch/research/research-groups/research-groups-a-z/own-content/unit/research-group-sebastian-hiller/hiller-cv |title=CV of Prof. Dr. Sebastian Hiller |publisher=unibas.ch/ |date= |accessdate=2024-10-07}}</ref>

== Life ==
Sebastian Hiller studied Interdisciplinary Natural Sciences at ETH Zurich and the University of Cambridge. He obtained his doctorate in 2006 in the laboratory of the Swiss Nobel Prize winner [[Kurt Wüthrich]] on methods of [[Nuclear magnetic resonance|Nuclear Magnetic Resonance]] (NMR) spectroscopy. He conducted postdoctoral research with [[Gerhard Wagner (physicist)|Gerhard Wagner]] at Harvard Medical School in Boston and with Beat Meier at ETH Zurich. In 2010, Sebastian Hiller was awarded an [[Swiss National Science Foundation|SNSF]] professorship at the Biozentrum of the University of Basel. In 2015 he was appointed Associate Professor and in 2022 Full Professor at the University of Basel.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.vibconferences.be/speaker/sebastian-hiller |title=Sebastian Hiller, Biography |publisher=vibconferences.be |date= |accessdate=2024-10-07}}</ref>

== Work ==
Sebastian Hiller uses [[NMR spectroscopy]] to investigate the structure and function of [[protein]]s, their interactions and underlying molecular mechanisms. By investigating the biophysical principles of molecular [[Chaperone (protein)|chaperone]] function, he was recently able to show how the state of [[Alpha-synuclein|α-synuclein]] in living cells is regulated, which plays a key role in the development of [[Parkinson's disease]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=Regulation of α-synuclein by chaperones in mammalian cells |doi=10.1038/s41586-019-1808-9 |pmid=31802003 |volume=577 |issue=7788 |journal=Nature |pages=127–132 |year=2020 |last1=Burmann |first1=Björn M. |last2=Gerez |first2=Juan A. |last3=Matečko-Burmann |first3=Irena |last4=Campioni |first4=Silvia |last5=Kumari |first5=Pratibha |last6=Ghosh |first6=Dhiman |last7=Mazur |first7=Adam |last8=Aspholm |first8=Emelie |last9=Šulskis |first9=Darius |last10=Wawrzyniuk |first10=Magdalena |last11=Bock |first11=Thomas |last12=Schmidt |first12=Alexander |last13=Rüdiger |first13=Stefan G D |last14=Riek |first14=Roland |last15=Hiller |first15=Sebastian|pmc=6930850 }}</ref> He is also exploring the outer membrane protein [[Spontaneous generation|biogenesis]] of Gram-negative bacteria and the way it can be targeted by novel antibiotics. By elucidating the natural compound darobactin's mode of action, his research serves as a basis for the rational design of new antibiotics, to help fight the world-wide antimicrobial resistance crisis.<ref>{{cite journal |title=The antibiotic darobactin mimics a β-strand to inhibit outer membrane insertase |doi=10.1038/s41586-021-03455-w |pmid=33854236 |volume=593 |issue=7857 |journal=Nature |pages=125–129 |year=2021 |last1=Kaur|first1=Hundeep |last2=Jakob |first2=Roman P |last3=Marzinek |first3=Jan K |last4=Green |first4=Robert |last5=Imai |first5=Yu |last6=Bolla |first6=Jani Reddy |last7=Agustoni |first7=Elia |last8=Robinson |first8=Carol V |last9=Bond |first9=Peter J |last10=Lewis |first10=Kim |last11=Maier |first11=Timm |last12=Hiller |first12=Sebastian|bibcode=2021Natur.593..125K }}</ref> Other areas of research focus on mechanisms of bacterial cell signaling and mechanisms that control pyroptosis and chronic inflammation. Recent findings showed that the protein [[NINJ1]] plays an important role in inflammatory reactions in the body and forms a molecular built-in breaking point on the cell membrane in preparation for cell death.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Structural basis of NINJ1-mediated plasma membrane rupture in cell death |doi=10.1038/s41586-023-05991-z |pmid=37198476 |volume=618 |issue=7967 |journal=Nature |pages=1065–1071 |year=2023 |last1=Degen|first1=Morris |last2=Santos |first2=José Carlos |last3=Pluhackova |first3=Kristyna |last4=Cebrero |first4=Gonzalo |last5=Ramos |first5=Saray |last6=Jankevicius |first6=Gytis |last7=Hartenian |first7=Ella |last8=Guillerm |first8=Undina |last9=Mari |first9=Stefania A |last10=Kohl |first10=Bastian |last11=Müller |first11=Daniel J |last12=Schanda |first12=Paul |last13=Maier |first13=Timm |last14=Perez |first14=Camilo |last15=Sieben |first15=Christian |last16=Broz |first16=Peter |last17=Hiller |first17=Sebastian|pmc=10307626 |bibcode=2023Natur.618.1065D }}</ref>
